subject: DPA & backup/log retention clarifications for MediPrime
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@mediprime.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: it-ops@mediprime.com
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA: backup purge and log exception questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams are reviewing the draft DPA and have a few specific questions about Redwood's retention and backup purge practices before we proceed with signature:

1) Backup prune/purge cadence: you mention backups are retained for "X" period in the draft. Can you confirm the exact purge cadence for full system backups and incremental backups (time-to-purge after snapshot creation)? We need a vendor schedule to map to our archival policy.

2) Cross-border backups: Does Redwood replicate or move backups outside the data region? If yes, where are backups stored for US-region customers and what controls are applied?

3) Log retention exceptions: we have a regulatory requirement to keep certain audit trails for 7 years, but we also have scoped debug logs that we want to shorter-retain. Is there an exception process to retain or extend log retention for specific accounts or timeboxed investigations? What is the SLA for approval?

4) Subprocessors & KMS: please provide the current list of subprocessors that may touch backups or logs and confirm whether customer data in backups is encrypted with a customer-managed key (CMK) or Redwood-managed key.

We've attached our internal checklist and the redline of the DPA for reference. Appreciate a response by end of day Tuesday so we can keep the procurement window open.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Senior Counsel — Privacy & Security
MediPrime

Attachments: MediPrime_DPA_redline_v1.docx, mp-retention-checklist.pdf

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-09T12:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: backup purge and log exception questions

Olivia,

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on what you need. High level answers below; I've cc'd Legal (Kimberly), Contracts (Karthik) and Privacy (Marissa) to confirm and add contract language where needed. I'll attach a proposed backup purge schedule (CSV) and a redline to the DPA.

1) Backup purge cadence
- Full snapshots: retained for 90 days from creation then purged unless flagged for escrow.
- Incremental/differential snapshots: retained for 30 days.
- Cold archives: customer-requested exports moved to cold storage retained for 365 days from export date unless a longer retention is requested and mutually agreed.
- Purge window: purges run in weekly batches for each region; deletion is irreversible 48 hours after the purge job completes.

2) Cross-border backups
- For US-region tenants, primary backups remain in-region (us-east-1/us-west-2). We do replicate metadata and replication checkpoints to a DR region (also within the US by default).
- No automatic cross-border copies for US-region customers unless enabled via a contractual addendum; if you require geo-redundancy to EU/APAC, we surface that as an opt-in with documented subprocessors and controls.

3) Log retention exceptions process
- Default log retention: 365 days for standard operational logs; 180 days for high-volume debug traces.
- Exception process: customers may request a timeboxed extension for specified log types via a formal evidence request (ticket + audit justification). Requests are reviewed by Privacy + Security and typically resolved within 5 business days.
- For regulatory holds (e.g., subpoena or audit) we will implement a temporary preservation hold that prevents purge jobs for the scope/time requested; hold confirmation and narrow scope are required.

4) Subprocessors & KMS
- Current subprocessors touching backups: AWS S3 (storage), Google Cloud Storage (cold export partner), FastLane Backup Services (managed tape/archival partner). We will provide a current subprocessor list in the DPA exhibit.
- Encryption: backups are encrypted at-rest with Redwood-managed keys by default. Customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS are available for Dedicated and Private customers; for hosted accounts we can discuss a Bring-Your-Key (BYK) program under an enterprise addendum.

Next steps:
- I attached redwood_backup_schedule_v1.csv with purge windows and a proposed DPA redline (MediPrime_DPA_redline_v2.docx). Can you confirm whether MediPrime needs: (a) shorter backup retention for specific data classes, or (b) CMK for hosted backups?
- Karthik/Kimberly: please review the DPA redline for the exceptions language and subprocessor exhibit we plan to attach.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_backup_schedule_v1.csv, MediPrime_DPA_redline_v2.docx

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@mediprime.com>

Date: 2026-08-10T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: backup purge and log exception questions

Stephanie —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the CSV. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing:

• We are aiming to classify backups by data sensitivity. For PHI-containing dumps we'd like a 45-day purge for full snapshots (not 90). Is that feasible as a scoped carveout?
• We need the subprocessor list in the DPA exhibit BEFORE signature — can you provide a snapshot of the current list and a change-notification cadence (how far in advance Redwood notifies us of new subprocessors)?
• For logs: the 5-business-day exception SLA is reasonable; can you add a written commitment that preservation holds will be processed within 48 hours for investigations flagged by Redwood Security (i.e., we don't want to wait on our ticket to be approved if Redwood flags an incident affecting our tenant)?
• KMS: MediPrime requires CMK for backups containing PHI. If BYK is not available for hosted yet, we need a path and timeline to enable CMK prior to go-live.

Quoted for context — your original:
> - Full snapshots: retained for 90 days from creation then purged unless flagged for escrow.
> - Incremental/differential snapshots: retained for 30 days.

Please let us know whether the PHI 45-day carveout and 48-hour hold acknowledgment are acceptable. If so we'll move the DPA redline forward and schedule a short legal-ops call.

Thanks,
Olivia

Subject: Re: DPA: backup purge and log exception questions — proposed contract language

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear asks. Karthik and I reviewed Stephanie's response and propose the following to put in the DPA redline and an exhibit: 

• PHI carveout: Redwood will support a scoped retention override for predefined data classes (e.g., PHI) with a maximum default of 45 days for full snapshots. This will be documented as an optional exhibit where the customer selects the classes and retention periods at onboarding.

• Subprocessor notice: Redwood commits to a 30-day advance notice for non-critical subprocessors and immediate notice for security-impacting changes (as defined in Exhibit B). The current subprocessor list will be attached in Exhibit A as of the DPA signature date; Redwood will maintain an online subprocessor register and provide a monthly snapshot link to MediPrime.

• Preservation holds: Redwood commits to process preservation holds requested by Redwood Security within 48 hours when the hold is a result of a Redwood-identified incident that materially impacts the customer's tenant; customer-requested holds will follow the standard 5-business-day review SLA. We will add language to the DPA to reflect both pathways and the evidence required for each.

• KMS path: Redwood confirms CMK support for Dedicated/Private now, and for hosted we will provide a BYK roadmap with milestones. We propose including a timeline clause: BYK available for hosted accounts within 90–120 days after enterprise activation and an interim escrow-based approach if necessary.

Karthik — please prepare the DPA redline with the exhibit templates and the subprocessor register link. Marissa — please confirm any privacy/eval notes for the PHI carveout (audit logs required, access controls).

Olivia — once we share the updated redline I'll propose a 30-minute call to walk through the exhibits.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal — Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
